## W0-4e / W0-4f / W0-4g: R-W04 follow-ups (backfill cap exemption, ues soups on the pool, pool instrumentation)

Everything sits under the EXISTING `ENABLE_PRICE_PARSE_OFFLOAD` (default OFF, read per call). There is no new flag, and the knob `PRICE_PARSE_MAX_WORKERS` is unchanged. With the flag OFF, behaviour is byte-identical to `61585c58`.

### Defects
- **W0-4e.** Under the flag, `curl_fetch_html` capped every caller at `PRICE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES` (3,000,000 chars). That included `_lazy_bh_pdp_backfill`, whose `re.findall(href=.../product/...)` over a curled retailer SEARCH page then missed any href past 3,000,000 chars (R-W04 ruling 5, disclosed). The scan also ran inline on the event loop.
- **W0-4f.** `url_extraction_service.extract_from_url` built one or more BeautifulSoup trees inline on the event loop in both flag states, via `extract_amazon_data`, `extract_noon_data` or `extract_generic_data`. It was the one entry in the transitive AST guard's allowlist (R-W04 ruling 8).
- **W0-4g.** CLAUDE.md W0 activation step (2) says to watch the price-parse pool's queue depth, but nothing exposed it. Separately, four r1 adversary mutants survived the existing pins.

### Design
- **`price_service.curl_fetch_html(url, *, cap=True)`.** The new parameter is keyword-only. Under the flag, `cap=True` returns `resp.text[:PRICE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES]` and `cap=False` returns the whole body. With the flag OFF, `cap` is never read and the whole body is returned. `_lazy_bh_pdp_backfill` is the ONLY `cap=False` caller in `app/`, and an AST pin enforces that.
- **`_lazy_bh_pdp_backfill`.** The pure-sync `re.findall` over the body moves into one nested block, `_w04_scan_block()`. ## W0-4e / W0-4f / W0-4g — R-W04 follow-ups under the existing ENABLE_PRICE_PARSE_OFFLOAD

### Defects
- **W0-4e.** Under the flag, `curl_fetch_html` capped every caller at PRICE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES (3,000,000 chars). As a result, `structured_comparison_service._lazy_bh_pdp_backfill`'s `re.findall` over a retailer SEARCH page lost any /product/ href past 3 MB (R-W04 ruling 5). The scan also ran inline on the loop.
- **W0-4f.** `url_extraction_service.extract_from_url` ran `extract_amazon_data` / `extract_noon_data` / `extract_generic_data` (each builds one or more BeautifulSoup) inline on the event loop in both flag states (R-W04 ruling 8). The transitive AST guard allowlisted it.
- **W0-4g.** CLAUDE.md activation step (2) says to watch the price-parse pool's queue depth, but nothing exposed it.

### Design (all under the EXISTING flag, read per call; no new flag)
- **e.** `price_service.curl_fetch_html(url, *, cap=True)`: under the flag, `resp.text[:PRICE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES] if cap else resp.text`. Flag OFF: the whole body, and `cap` is never read. `_lazy_bh_pdp_backfill` is the ONLY `cap=False` site in app/ (AST-pinned). It moves its pure-sync `re.findall` into one nested block. Under the flag the block runs on the price-parse pool through `from app.services import price_service as _w04_ps; await _w04_ps.run_parse_offloaded(...)`; flag OFF it runs inline. The `_accept` loop stays on the event loop in both states.
- **f.** The extractor is selected as a module global at call time. Under the flag, `html = html[:PRICE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES]` (the same capped html then reaches `extract_with_ai`) and `raw_data = await _w04_ps.run_parse_offloaded(_extractor, html, url)`, with price_service resolved through the package attribute (#185). Flag OFF: `_extractor(html, url)` inline on the whole body. Extractor exceptions propagate with the same type in both states. `_TRANSITIVE_ALLOWLIST` is now `frozenset()`.
- **g.** `_PRICE_PARSE_STATS` counters are maintained by `run_parse_offloaded`:
  - `waiting` (and `peak_waiting`) is counted only when `sem.locked()` right before `await sem.acquire()`, i.e. the job is blocked on the semaphore. It is decremented in a finally around the acquire.
  - `running`, `jobs_total` and `peak_running` are updated after the acquire.
  - `running -= 1` and `sem.release()` happen in the finally around the executor await (the `async with sem` contract, now pinned directly, see Gates).
  - `price_service.price_parse_pool_stats()` returns None until the pool exists.
  - `_get_price_parse_pool` logs ONE `[PRICE-PARSE] pool built workers=N` INFO line when it builds the pool.
  - `app.main.price_parse_pool_snapshot()` reads `sys.modules` (never an import), catches any stats error, and returns `{}` or `{"price_parse_pool": stats}`. `/health` merges it; there is no await or I/O in the handler.

### Flag row
- **Flag:** ENABLE_PRICE_PARSE_OFFLOAD, default OFF, accepts true/1/yes/on (case- and space-insensitive), read per call.
- **Effect ON:** the backfill scan sees the whole search page and runs on the pool; the three ues extractors run on the pool over a 3 MB-capped input; `/health.price_parse_pool` appears once the pool is built.
- **OFF:** byte-identical.
  - Corpus OFF (R-W04's four-flag list) reproduces OVERALL 9504e5a94a218969764c8cbfdb43243da7bfcd8e0950bb5fb9148b9a9258ce99 in 9m49s.
  - ON `--compare` gives results a1b3460c28579fab605287e1b5a05dd9cb8a3b07782573dfb5aac005104c59d8 on both sides, equal=True, DIFFERING RECORDS 0 of 1656, in 2m54s.
  - Flag OFF, the pool is never built, so the `/health` key is absent and /health is unchanged.
- **Knob:** PRICE_PARSE_MAX_WORKERS (default 4) is unchanged and read once, when the pool is built.

### /health key contract
- `price_parse_pool` is absent until the pool exists. Then it is `{workers, queued, waiting, running, jobs_total, peak_waiting, peak_running}`.
- `waiting` counts jobs blocked on the submission semaphore. `peak_waiting >= 1` means queueing happened; one uncontended parse reads peak_waiting 0.
- `queued` is the executor's own work-queue depth. It stays 0 while every awaited parse holds a slot. It is NOT "0 by construction": a cancelled await (any `asyncio.wait_for` cap, e.g. the 15 s price race or STREAM_HARD_CAP) releases its slot and decrements `running` while its parse keeps its pool thread. So `queued > 0` means orphaned parses from cancelled awaits are occupying pool threads, not a broken semaphore. `running` counts awaited jobs only and under-reports occupancy while orphans run.
- Measured and pinned on a size-1 pool: cancel A mid-parse, then submit B, and the stats read `{running: 1, waiting: 0, queued: 1}`.

### Stated limits

- The corpus harness calls `extract_price_from_html` directly, so it observes neither the cap nor the W0-4c/e/f sites.

  - W0-4e: the backfill is exempt from the curl cap via `cap=False` and its scan is offloaded.

### Defects
- **W0-4e.** Under the flag, `curl_fetch_html` capped EVERY caller at `PRICE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES` (3,000,000 chars), including `structured_comparison_service._lazy_bh_pdp_backfill`, which regex-scans a curled retailer SEARCH page for an in-domain `/product/` href. So an href past 3,000,000 chars was silently lost, flag ON only (R-W04 ruling 5, disclosed there). The existing pin covered flag OFF only.
- **W0-4f.** `url_extraction_service.extract_from_url` ran `extract_amazon_data` / `extract_noon_data` / `extract_generic_data` INLINE on the event loop in both flag states. Each builds one or more `BeautifulSoup` trees; generic builds two. The transitive AST guard carried an allowlist entry for exactly this.
- **W0-4g.** CLAUDE.md's W0 activation step (2) says to watch the price-parse pool's queue depth, but nothing exposed it. Separately, the R-W04 r1 adversary left four test-side gaps (below).

### Design
- **W0-4e.**
  - `curl_fetch_html(url, *, cap=True)`: a keyword-only exemption. Under the flag, `cap=False` returns the whole `resp.text`. Flag OFF, the kwarg is never read (the base statements).
  - `_lazy_bh_pdp_backfill` is the ONLY `cap=False` site in `app/` (AST-pinned).
  - Its `re.findall` is ONE nested block, `_w04_scan_block()`. Under the flag it runs through `price_service.run_parse_offloaded`, with price_service resolved as the package attribute at call time. Flag OFF, the identical block runs inline.
  - The `_accept` loop (`validate_scrape_url`, `score_source`, ordering) stays on the event loop in both states.
  - **Effect: correctness only** (see stated limits). The href past 3 MB is found again under the flag.
- **W0-4f.**
  - The extractor is selected as a module global at call time.
  - Under the flag: `from app.services import price_service as _w04_ps`, the same package-attribute form scs uses (ruling R2). Then `html = html[:_w04_ps.PRICE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES]`, one truncation right after the fetch; the SAME capped html also reaches `extract_with_ai`, mirroring the render legs (bounded parse input, unbounded fetch). Then `raw_data = await _w04_ps.run_parse_offloaded(_extractor, html, url)`.
  - Flag OFF: `_extractor(html, url)` inline on the whole body.
  - An extractor exception propagates with the same type in both states.
  - `_TRANSITIVE_ALLOWLIST` in `tests/test_retro_w0_4.py` is now `frozenset()`.
  - **Measured effect:** a 2.7 MB generic page parse costs the loop a max 0.28-1.03 s gap offloaded, against 7.4-9.2 s inline.
- **W0-4g.**
  - `price_service._PRICE_PARSE_STATS` holds `{jobs_total, waiting, running, peak_waiting, peak_running}`, mutated only in `run_parse_offloaded` on the loop thread.
  - `waiting` counts a job only when it is BLOCKED on the submission semaphore: `sem.locked()` is checked right before `await sem.acquire()`, and the count is decremented in a finally around the acquire. A cancelled waiter never leaks a count or releases a slot it did not take.
  - `running` / `jobs_total` count after the acquire. `running -= 1` and `sem.release()` sit in the finally around the executor await.
  - `price_parse_pool_stats()` is a pure read: `None` until the pool exists, otherwise a FRESH dict `{workers, queued, **counters}`.
  - `_get_price_parse_pool` logs ONE grep-stable line when it builds the pool: `[PRICE-PARSE] pool built workers=N`.
  - `app/main.py::price_parse_pool_snapshot()` reads `sys.modules.get("app.services.price_service")` (never an import), catches every `Exception` into `{}`, and `/health` merges `**price_parse_pool_snapshot()`. The handler stays a pure dict read: no await, no import, none of the forbidden substrings.

### Flag row
| | |
|---|---|
| Flag | `ENABLE_PRICE_PARSE_OFFLOAD`, EXISTING, default OFF, read per call by the three agreeing readers |
| Effect ON | the backfill scan sees the whole search page; the ues extractors run on the price-parse pool with the parse input capped at 3,000,000 chars; `/health` carries `price_parse_pool` once the pool is built |
| OFF | byte-identical: the pool is never built, so the `/health` key is absent |
| Knobs | `PRICE_PARSE_MAX_WORKERS` (default 4, clamped 1..16, read once at pool build) |

### /health key contract
- `price_parse_pool` is **absent** until the pool exists, so it is always absent flag OFF.
- Once the pool exists it reads `{workers, queued, waiting, running, jobs_total, peak_waiting, peak_running}`.
  - `waiting` = parses blocked on the submission semaphore.
  - `peak_waiting >= 1` means queueing happened at least once (one uncontended parse reads `peak_waiting 0`, per ruling R1).
  - `queued` = the executor's own work-queue depth. **It is transiently non-zero on an ordinary semaphore hand-off**, because the next job is submitted before a pool thread has dequeued it. Measured with no cancellation anywhere: 1-3 of 60 samples at 2 and 4 workers, up to `queued 2`. So a single sample means nothing. A `queued > 0` that **persists across polls** means orphaned parses: a cancelled await, such as a wait_for cap firing, releases its slot while its parse keeps its thread, and `running` counts awaited jobs only, so it under-reports occupancy then (pinned with a size-1 pool).

### Stated limits
- **W0-4e's offload does NOT free the event loop.** CPython's `re` holds the GIL for the whole `findall`. Measured on a 30 MB page: max loop gap 0.147 s offloaded vs 0.153 s inline, against 0.017 s for an offloaded `time.sleep` control. The adversary measured 0.95 s vs 0.91 s on 54 MB.

- `fetch_page` (httpx, ues) is uncapped in both states.

A window that finds nothing advances to `max(pos, min(last_quote_in_window, endpos) - 5)`, because a match holds no quote except its two delimiters. The window doubles when stuck.
